question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract, document Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external pattern, or defer this broad work to narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The missing distributed backend is clear in source, but the backend boundary, config shape, worker failure semantics, credential model, observability surface, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and plugin/core ownership before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

options.title: Document External Pattern
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's built-in runtime single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Let the cron HA, external session storage, and distributed runtime issues settle first, then revisit whether a broader distributed worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and plugin/core ownership before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.
